process_issues.description: The diagnostic shim assumed the failure path was: HTTP error -> assertOk throws AppError -> our catch surfaces SnackBar. Manual smoke proves that assumption is false — the failure is on a path the shim does not cover. Likely candidates: (1) the picker dialog never returns a selected member (so onAdd is never invoked); (2) the POST succeeds with HTTP 200 but the returned collaborator list is empty or omits the AI user (no exception, silent state mismatch); (3) the failure happens in a parallel entry point (agent bubble overlay, sync orchestrator) the shim did not touch; (4) BuildContext used for ScaffoldMessenger is invalid (dialog Navigator pops first), so showSnackBar is a no-op against an unmounted messenger.
process_issues.lesson: When shipping a 'diagnostic shim' meant to surface unknown failures, the shim must be validated against the actual failure path before claiming PASS. Widget tests pass when fed an explicit AppError throw — that proves the shim works for the contract-test path, NOT for the unknown production failure. The verification-gate evidence for #651 should have included a manual smoke confirming the shim fires against a known-bad input (e.g. point ServerConfigService at a deliberately wrong URL and confirm the SnackBar appears), not just the green contract test.

process_issues.description: PR #651 shipped a release (v18.38) without an instrumented smoke that actually triggered a failure mode the shim claimed to cover. The pre-handoff verification step in the orchestrator (6b) was deferred to user manual smoke because the failure mode is production-side; but for a diagnostic shim that is itself the deliverable, a Computer-Use smoke pointing at a deliberately misconfigured server would have caught this before the release tag.
process_issues.lesson: For diagnostic shims, the shim's TRIGGER condition must be tested live, not just unit-tested. Computer-Use smoke with intentional misconfiguration is the cheapest way.
